To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the teacher's positioning of students as kinds is mediated by the curricular resources and activities of the classroom and that the positioning of students as different kinds of learners is related to their social identities and to their participation in classroom activity.

students are positioned as kinds of learners through teacher formulations of curricular goals and objectives, curricular tools and affordances, and participation patterns, which influence how different ways of learning and participating are recognized and evaluated across interactions.
students are positioned as different kinds of persons and activity through the mediation of classroom interactions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ways in which the micro- and macro-levels of social life are intertwined and how they are mediated by curricular resources.

understanding the ways that positioning and the resources that positionings draw upon, are both constitutive of the ways that students are positioned and how they position themselves in the classroom.
the ways that the social and ideological resources for classroom positioning mediate micro-identities and macro-kinds, as well as how these processes influence the ways that learning is organized.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the study of positioning theory is an important and useful approach to understanding the complex ways in which individuals are positioned in and by social interactions.

the analysis of classroom positioning provides a useful way to understand the ways that students’ participation is mediated by the social and material context, and that this mediation has consequences for how students learn and how their participation is valued.

the study contributes to positioning analysis by demonstrating that acts of positioning are mediated by the social and material context in which they occur, and by demonstrating the ways in which these acts of positioning construct and are constructed by ideologies of knowing and being.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ways in which we position students and the ways we mediate those positions are not neutral.

the ideological and material resources that mediate classroom interactions, such as curricular tools and teacher formulations of goals, afford opportunities for positioning that influence how students participate and are positioned.
the micro- and macro-level resources that mediate classroom interactions are not only mutually constitutive, but also mutually informing of each other.
The main takeaway from our work is that
positioning theory offers a productive lens for understanding the social and material resources that mediate opportunities to participate and learn.
we can use positioning theory to examine how the micro-, meso- and macro-social levels of analysis are mutually constitutive of the social and curricular practices of learning.
positioning theory can be fruitfully extended by considering how the ideological work of macro-structures and micro-interactions intersect in the mediation of identity and activity.
